There is no point in this pipeline's 30+ year history that the 500 MMcf/d figure matches cleanly; it reads as either a stale mid-life figure or a transcription error. I'm proposing 1,500 MMcf/d (TC Energy's own stated figure, cross-checked against two independent sources landing in the same 1.5-1.7 Bcf/d band) as the corrected value; note the small ~1.5-1.7 spread across sources reflects different measurement conventions (design vs. physical receipt capability) and should be resolved by whoever applies this against the live FERC tariff if greater precision is wanted.

The Corning<->Ramapo routing for THIS built segment is independently confirmed by: Oil & Gas Journal ('186-mile Corning-Ramapo section'/'182-mile' pipeline, 'originates ... Southern Tier ... Corning'), Energy Intelligence ('Connects Empire Connector system at Corning, New York to Algonquin system at Ramapo, New York'), and NiSource's FY2007 10-K SEC filing ('connects Empire pipeline near Corning, NY and extends eastward to interconnect with Algonquin at Ramapo, NY'). resolutions.researcher_notes: The row exists and is real (FERC Docket No. CP18-89-000, 'Empire North Project'), but its recorded LengthKnown=40.20 km (25 mi) and Diameter=26.00 in do not match any physical pipe FERC or the operator describes for this project -- the project built ZERO new mainline pipe. Five independent-of-each-other documents agree on the facility list: (1) FERC's own Notice of Intent to Prepare an EA (Federal Register 2018-07924, filed/opened Feb. 16, 2018): 'The Empire North Project would consist of the following facilities: A new 21,000 horsepower (hp) compressor station in Jackson Township, Tioga County, Pennsylvania; a new 32,000 hp compressor station in the Town of Farmington, Ontario County, New York; modifications of the existing regulator valves and station piping and installation of metering facilities at the existing New Victor Regulator Station...; minor modifications to the existing Jackson Meter and Regulator Station...; and upgrading the maximum allowable operating pressure of the Empire Connector Pipeline (ECP) from 1,290 psig to 1,440 psig. The ECP is an existing 76.6-mile-long, 24-inch-diameter pipeline that runs from Victor, New York to Corning, New York' -- i.e. the only pipe named is a DIFFERENT, already-existing, already-counted (on the Main Line row, P0288) segment with a different length (76.6 mi, not 25) and different diameter (24 in, not 26), in a different state (wholly within New York, not PA-to-Ontario). Total land disturbance for the whole project is stated as 50.4 acres -- consistent with two compressor-station sites, not with 25 miles of new linear pipeline construction (which would run to hundreds of acres of temporary ROW). (2) National Fuel's own official 'Empire North Project Fact Sheet' PDF (nationalfuel.com): the facilities list is two new compressor stations + two 'minor modifications' to existing stations + an MAOP uprate on the existing ECP explicitly noted as 'not expected to require any construction-related activities' -- no pipeline mileage anywhere in the facility list. (3) National Fuel's own SEC 8-K investor-presentation exhibit (2019, EDGAR accession 0001193125-19-280494) states outright: 'No new pipeline construction' -- the company's own securities filing, under legal disclosure obligations, using that exact phrase; infrastructure is described as '2 new compressor stations in NY (1) & Pa. (1)'. (4) National Fuel's own current, FERC-effective Empire Pipeline Gas Tariff (effective Sept. 15, 2020, and still governing rates as of the version searched) defines, at Section 1.19 of its General Terms and Conditions: '"Empire North Capacity" shall mean firm transportation capacity resulting from Transporter's incremental facility expansion project authorized in Commission Docket No. CP18-89-000' -- the tariff's own vocabulary treats 'Empire North' purely as a CAPACITY product (paired with an 'Empire North Compressor Fuel Retention' percentage), never as a named physical pipeline segment, in contrast to how the same tariff names the 'Original Empire Pipeline' and the 'Empire Connector' as actual physical assets. (5) A peer deep-sweep shard on this same wiki page's other GEM row (P0288, Empire Pipeline Main Line, in this same batch) independently reached the identical conclusion from its own research and flagged it as a cross-row lead for this exact row, quoting nationalfuel.com's current 'About Empire Pipeline' page: 'In 2020 Empire placed the Empire North Project into service, which saw the construction of two new compressor stations...' with no mention of new pipe. The apparent origin of the erroneous 40.2 km/26 in figures: RBN Energy's project data card for 'Empire North Expansion' (archived, since the live page 403s bots) lists 'Diameter: 26 inches' and 'Length: 25 miles' alongside Origin: Jackson, PA and Destination: Chippawa, ON -- these numbers match the sheet's LengthKnown/Diameter EXACTLY, strongly suggesting RBN Energy's card (via gem.wiki's citation of it) is the sheet's source, and RBN's card appears to describe the general PA-to-Ontario corridor over which the new/uprated capacity flows, not the footprint of new construction. Per this sweep's own standing convention (already applied in this same batch to Rockies Express Zone 3 East-to-West, and to the len-0 Rover phases/Vector P3202): an expansion project that adds capacity via compression/reversal with no new mainline pipe gets LengthKnown=0, Diameter blank -- that convention applies squarely here. Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, StartYear1=2020, and the PA/Ontario endpoints are all independently confirmed (see fills[] below) and are NOT in question -- only the physical Length/Diameter attribution is wrong.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage System (EGTS)
resolutions.recommendation: Adjudicate against P0176 'Dominion Gas Pipeline' (6,059 mi, cap 7,200 MMcf/d, 'Dominion LNG in Maryland, gas from Ohio and Virginia -> New United Kingdom'). Both rows describe the same corporate lineage of Appalachian/Mid-Atlantic FERC-regulated gas transmission assets under different names: the entity now called Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. (EGTS) is the direct rename of Dominion Energy Transmission -- Berkshire Hathaway Energy acquired Dominion's gas transmission/storage business Nov. 1, 2020 and renamed the former CNG/Dominion operations 'Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage' (operator's own history page). P0176's segment description ('gas from Ohio and Virginia', feeding Dominion's Cove Point LNG in Maryland) matches EGTS's confirmed footprint (Ohio, Virginia, Maryland among its six states of operation). The two rows' capacities (7,200 vs 9,500 MMcf/d) and lengths (6,059 mi vs ~4,000 mi/6,437.38 km) do not match exactly, which could reflect different measurement vintages/scopes (P0176 last updated 2023-08-11 vs P3220 2022-10-07) or could mean P0176 bundles additional assets (e.g. the Cove Point feeder/LNG-adjacent capacity) that EGTS's core transmission-and-storage figure does not. Not resolved without reading P0176's own sources directly -- flagging for human adjudication rather than asserting identity.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Checked the operator's own corporate-history page (bhegts.com/our-businesses/EGTS): 'The companies that would become Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage are born of an important by-product of ... Standard Oil' -> Hope Natural Gas (1898) -> Consolidated Natural Gas / CNG Transmission -> Dominion Resources merger (2000) -> 'On November 1, 2020, Berkshire Hathaway Energy acquires a number of Dominion Energy gas transmission, storage, and LNG assets ... The company is now called BHE GT&S, and the former CNG operations are known as Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage.' This directly documents that EGTS = the renamed former Dominion Energy Transmission network. Given P0176 in the roster is literally named 'Dominion Gas Pipeline' and its segment text references Ohio/Virginia gas feeding a Maryland LNG facility (Cove Point, also a BHE GT&S business line), the two rows plausibly encode the same underlying network pre- and post-rename. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: this row (P5830, docket CP14-498-000) is textually and docket-wise distinct from the other two Rockies Express rows -- P5829 ('Seneca Lateral', a SEPARATE upstream lateral in Noble/Monroe Counties OH, dockets CP13-539/CP14-194/CP15-102) and P5831 ('Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement', a SEPARATE, later, compression-only project, docket CP15-137, filed March 2015, in service Jan 2017); no merge action needed -- confirms and closes out the cross-row lead P5829's own shard flagged pointing at this docket. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- EIA's own 'Pipeline Type' field records 'Interstate' under FERC authority, and the company filings describe this as an NGA-jurisdictional mainline facility, not gathering/distribution. RouteType='Bidirectionality upgrade only' / RouteAccuracy='no route' (both already on the sheet) are CORRECT and should NOT be changed -- every source confirms this project reversed flow direction and added delivery-point capacity on EXISTING pipe, explicitly 'without the addition of incremental compression horsepower or pipeline looping,' so there is no new route to map. Opened and read to exhaustion: both Tallgrass-family 8-K exhibits (d177254dex992.htm and the REX FY2015 GAAP financial statements exhibit a991rex20151231gaapfinanci.htm), the TEP FY2017 10-K (which separately names 'Tallgrass NatGas Operator, LLC' as REX's day-to-day operator -- see the Operator fill note below for how this reconciles with 'Rockies Express Pipeline LLC'), the TGE FY2019 10-K, the Phillips 66 FY2018 10-K, the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (downloaded and parsed directly, not just cited from the wiki pool), and the English Wikipedia article. resolutions.recommendation: Change Capacity from 1800.00 to 1200.00 MMcf/d. The sheet's current 1800 MMcf/d appears to be the resulting TOTAL/aggregate Zone 3 bi-directional capacity after this project completed (0.6 Bcf/d already added by the separately-recorded Seneca Lateral, P5829, plus this project's own 1.2 Bcf/d = 1.8 Bcf/d combined), not this project's own incremental capacity addition.
resolutions.researcher_notes: TWO independent origins both explicitly describe this project's OWN incremental addition as 1.2 Bcf/d (1200 MMcf/d), not 1.8 Bcf/d: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook records 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 1200 for the identically-named 'Zone 3 East-to-West Project' row (docket CP14-498, matching this row's docket exactly); (2) the Tallgrass corporate family's own SEC filings state twice, in near-identical language across two separate 8-K exhibits: 'The Zone 3 East-to-West Project was placed into commercial service on August 1, 2015 and creates an additional 1.2 million Dth per day of firm takeaway capacity from the Utica and Marcellus Shale Plays and the Appalachian Basin' (1 million Dth/day = ~1 MMcf/d, so 1.2 million Dth/day = ~1200 MMcf/d). Separately, English Wikipedia narrates the SAME August 1, 2015 event as making 'Zone 3 of the mainline fully bi-directional with the ability to move approximately 1.8 billion cubic feet per day' -- this 1.8 Bcf/d is the resulting TOTAL Zone-3 east-to-west capability after the project (i.e., the pre-existing 0.6 Bcf/d Seneca Lateral capacity, GEM's own P5829, plus this project's 1.2 Bcf/d addition = 1.8 Bcf/d combined), not this project's own incremental contribution -- and is very likely the source of the sheet's current 1800 MMcf/d value. This is a clean case of an aggregate/system-level figure recorded on an individual segment/project row (the recurring GEM data-quality pattern flagged in this batch's scope guidance). P5831's own already-staged shard (Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement, docket CP15-137) independently reached the identical conclusion via its own cross-row lead pointed at this row, using a different source (Phillips 66's FY2018 10-K segment table) -- so this finding is now corroborated a fourth way. Recommending Capacity be corrected to 1200.00 MMcf/d.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED, independently, twice. This row is the REX Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project, FERC Docket CP15-137-000: filed 2015-03-31 for authorization to build (1) three new mainline compressor stations in Pickaway and Fayette Counties, Ohio and Decatur County, Indiana, (2) additional compression at an existing station in Muskingum County, Ohio, and (3) ancillary facilities -- to add 0.8 Bcf/d of east-to-west capacity within Zone 3 (Audrain County, MO <-> Clarington, OH). FERC issued the Certificate 2016-02-25; construction commenced 2016-03-14; placed in service for the full 0.8 Bcf/d on 2017-01-06. This is a genuinely separate, sequential FERC project from P5830's Zone 3 East-to-West reversal (docket CP14-498, completed 2015-09-01) -- NOT a duplicate: East-to-West made Zone 3 bi-directional first (adding 1.2 Bcf/d e-to-w per the company's own 8-K, bringing e-to-w capacity to 1.8 Bcf/d), then this Capacity Enhancement project layered on a further 0.8 Bcf/d of compression (to 2.6 Bcf/d total), confirmed via two independent origins: (a) Tallgrass Energy Partners/GP SEC filings (the pipeline's co-owner, an SEC-regulated disclosure) and (b) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracking workbook (a government database, independent of the operator), which carries this exact project under the name 'Pipeline Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement' -- an exact SegmentName match -- with Cost=$532M, Capacity=800 MMcf/d, Beg_State=OH, End_State=MO, Docket=CP15-137, all matching the sheet. CAVEAT (informational, not a concern): EIA's own project note flags a one-day-scale wrinkle -- 'REX Zone 3 reversal was mostly in service in December 2016. Small portion went in to service Jan. 6, 2017. EIA categorized all 800 Mmcf/d as completed in 2016' -- while Tallgrass's own 10-K states flatly '...placed in-service in January 2017.' GEM's StartYear1=2017 matches the company's own in-service date and the EIA note's Jan 6 2017 completion of the LAST portion, so it is the more precise answer; flagging only so a reviewer isn't surprised the EIA workbook's own 'Year In Service' column reads 2016 for the same row. CROSS-ROW LEAD filed separately for P5830 below: EIA's Additional Capacity for the Zone 3 East-to-West project (docket CP14-498) is 1200 MMcf/d (matching the company's own '1.2 Bcf/d' language), not the 1800 MMcf/d currently on P5830's Capacity cell -- 1800 appears to be the resulting TOTAL Zone 3 bi-directional capacity after that project (an aggregate/system figure), not the project's own incremental addition. resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed independent of GEM. This segment is Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company's Del-Mar Energy Pathway Project, FERC Docket No. CP18-548-000 (application filed 2018-09-14; FERC issued a positive Environmental Assessment May 2019 and a certificate order Dec 19, 2019, Eastern Shore Natural Gas Co., 169 FERC P61,228 (2019)). Confirmed independently by (1) FERC's own EA PDF (www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/CP18-548-EA.pdf), (2) Eastern Shore's own project-archive page (esng.com), (3) a 2019 PR Newswire release issued by parent Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (NYSE:CPK), and (4) Chesapeake Utilities' FY2021 SEC Form 10-K (sec.gov), which states the project 'was placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2021' and that 'Construction of the project began in January 2020.' CLASSIFICATION: correct -- FERC's own EA text (line ~3855 of the extracted PDF) states 'Eastern Shore currently operates the only interstate natural gas transmission [system]...', confirming Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission for an operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate line. DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate. Compared against the roster's other Eastern Shore rows: P0182 (732 mi mainline, 1959) is the pre-existing system; P2003 (40 mi, '2017 Expansion Project') is FERC Docket PF16-7-000/CP17-28-000, certificated Oct 2017, a wholly separate proceeding with its own segments (Fair Hill Loop, Jennersville Loop, Daleville Compressor, Seaford-Millsboro Connector) -- see cross_row_leads. P6003's own docket (CP18-548-000) and facility names (Georgetown East M&R Station, Woodside Loop, Hollymount M&R Station, East Sussex Extension, Somerset Extension) are distinct from both. CAVEAT 1 (minor, not flagged as a concern): the sheet's LengthKnown=20.00 mi is close to but not exact -- FERC's EA states the four segments total 'approximately 19.5 miles,' and the 10-K separately describes '6 miles of pipeline looping...13 miles of new mainline extension' (=19 mi). Both are within ~2.5-5% of the sheet value and both sources hedge with 'approximately,' so this is read as rounding, not a material disagreement. CAVEAT 2 (minor): Eastern Shore's own project page states the last facility (Somerset Extension) was placed in service 'September 2021,' while Chesapeake's 10-K describes the whole project as placed into service 'in the fourth quarter of 2021' (Oct-Dec). Both are Chesapeake's own documents and the discrepancy is a quarter/month rounding matter internal to the company's own reporting, not a dispute with an outside source -- GEM's StartYear1=2021 is correct either way. Opened and read to exhaustion: FERC CP18-548-EA.pdf (full text via pdftotext), esng.com project-archive page, esng.com home page, esng.com/project/2017-expansion/ (cross-row), PR Newswire release, Chesapeake Utilities FY2021 10-K (cpk-20211231.htm, searched for every 'Del-Mar'/'Del Mar' occurrence). Not opened: EIA Natural Gas Data landing page (generic, does not name this project) and the FracTracker national map article (checked -- does not mention Del-Mar or Eastern Shore by name, so it cannot serve as a ref for this row); the two harvested Natural Gas Intelligence links (bit.ly-free, naturalgasintel.com) both now 404 and were about the 2017 Expansion project, not this one, based on their headlines ('...Expansion Approval...', '...NatGas Expansion') -- not chased via Wayback since they route to P2003, not P6003.

resolutions.recommendation: verify SegmentCost against a primary source; the only cost figure independently located ($37 million, a 2019 pre-construction estimate) does not match the sheet's $46,000,000
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost=46,000,000 USD (no ref). The only project-specific cost figure I could locate anywhere is Chesapeake Utilities' own 2019 PR Newswire release: 'The projected cost of the project is approximately $37 million' (with 'anticipated annual gross margin...of $5.1 million'). Neither FERC's EA (environmental assessments do not typically state project cost) nor Chesapeake's FY2021 10-K states a single all-in capital cost for Del-Mar specifically (the 10-K instead gives a multi-year adjusted-gross-margin ramp: $0.731M in 2019, $2.462M in 2020, $4.584M in 2021, rising to ~$6.89M by 2023 -- revenue, not capex). $37M is also only a pre-construction ESTIMATE from the certificate-application stage, and the project ran roughly a year behind its original schedule (EA anticipated construction Sept 2019-Sept 2020; actual construction ran Jan 2020-Sept/Q4 2021), which is exactly the kind of delay that inflates realized cost above an early estimate -- so I cannot rule out that $46M is the correct final figure and $37M is simply stale. I searched Chesapeake's SEC filings (10-K text, financing-activities section) for a specific Del-Mar capex total and did not find one restated in later filings. Flagging as a spec concern with $37,000,000 as the only sourced candidate rather than silently accepting the sheet's $46,000,000, which is currently unsourced anywhere I could find. A researcher with access to Chesapeake's rate-case filings (Delaware PSC / Maryland PSC) or a later 10-K capex table could likely resolve this definitively; I did not chase state-PSC rate dockets given time budget.
